activities.name: THE CUBE
activities.style: Live version of the TV show
activities.whyGo: Twenty-one glass cubes across three floors, playing seven games out of the television show against the clock - the closest thing London has to being on it.
activities.opNote: Teams of four, booked in advance. Six bars and two kitchens on site, so spectators are catered for as well as players.

activities.name: Fairgame
activities.style: Reworked fairground games
activities.whyGo: Skee-Ball, Whac-A-Mole and roll-a-ball rebuilt at proper scale, with an RFID wristband keeping everyone's score so the competition never stops to do arithmetic.
activities.opNote: STRICTLY OVER 18 AT ALL TIMES - it looks like a family arcade and is not. Closed Mondays. Quieter and cheaper off-peak.

activities.name: Electric Shuffle
activities.style: Shuffleboard bar
activities.whyGo: Shuffleboard with the scoring and the game modes handled by a screen above the table, from the people behind Flight Club - semi-private booths rather than a room full of strangers.
activities.opNote: Tables booked by the hour. AGE POLICY AFTER A CERTAIN HOUR NEEDS VERIFYING - activity bars commonly go 18+ in the evening.

activities.name: Flip Out
activities.style: Indoor adventure park
activities.whyGo: Bumper cars, a roller rink, laser quest, drift trikes and toddler soft play under one roof in the shopping centre - the wet-weather answer for a family in Canary Wharf.
activities.opNote: DESPITE THE BRAND, THIS SITE HAS NO TRAMPOLINES. Flip Out is a trampoline-park chain and the Canary Wharf branch is not one - check the attraction list before promising a child a trampoline.

activities.name: Capital Karts
activities.style: Indoor go-karting
activities.whyGo: Indoor karting in Canary Wharf rather than out on an industrial estate, which is where this normally means going.
activities.opNote: MINIMUM AGE AND HEIGHT NEED VERIFYING - karting always has both and they decide whether a family can go at all.

activities.name: Canary Wharf Ice Rink
activities.style: Seasonal outdoor rink
activities.whyGo: London's longest-running seasonal rink, outdoors among the towers - the only time Canary Wharf is somewhere people come on purpose at the weekend.
activities.opNote: In CANADA SQUARE PARK, not Jubilee Park - they are a three-minute walk apart and guides mix them up. Runs late October to late February, so it is a four-month season rather than a Christmas pop-up.

activities.name: Crossrail Place Roof Garden
activities.style: Free covered garden
activities.whyGo: A planted garden under a timber lattice roof on top of the Elizabeth line station, split along the line of the Greenwich meridian with Asian planting on one side and American on the other.
activities.opNote: Free and open to the public. The most-cited thing to do in Canary Wharf across the local guides, and the one nobody expects to find here.

activities.name: GoBoat
activities.style: Self-drive electric boats
activities.whyGo: You drive it yourself - no licence needed - around the docks past Harbour Quay, Billingsgate and out towards the O2, with a table in the middle for a picnic.
activities.opNote: Priced per boat rather than per person, so it gets cheaper the fuller it is. Bring your own food. Weather-dependent.

activities.name: Pitch
activities.style: Simulator golf and bar
activities.whyGo: Screen golf in booked bays with a bar attached - the format that lets people who do not play golf spend an evening at it.
activities.opNote: Bays booked by the hour. EVENING AGE POLICY NEEDS VERIFYING.

activities.name: Billingsgate Fish Market
activities.style: Working wholesale fish market
activities.whyGo: The UK's largest inland fish market, trading before dawn a few minutes from the towers - the public can walk in and buy, and almost nobody does.
activities.opNote: OPENS AROUND 4AM AND IS DONE BY MID-MORNING, Tuesday to Saturday. Turning up at a civilised hour means an empty hall. LONG-TERM RELOCATION HAS BEEN ANNOUNCED - verify it is still trading here before publishing.

activities.name: Jubilee Park
activities.style: The estate's main green space
activities.whyGo: The largest green space in Canary Wharf - dawn redwoods, 22 fountains and a serpentine water channel by Jacques Wirtz, where the whole estate eats lunch the moment it is warm enough.
activities.opNote: Free, and you walk straight into it at street level. NOT A ROOF GARDEN, whatever the engineering says - it is built over the Jubilee line station box, but nobody experiences it that way. The roof garden you go UP to is Crossrail Place, which is a different place entirely.

activities.name: Illusionaries
activities.style: Story-based digital art
activities.whyGo: Three galleries of 360-degree projection and sound built as a single 40-minute story rather than a set of photo backdrops - billed as the UK's first narrative immersive art experience.
activities.opNote: TEMPORARY VENUE showing rotating exhibitions - the opening show was 'Memories of a Dead Poet' by Arash Irandoust. VERIFY WHAT IS CURRENTLY SHOWING, and that it is still open at all, before publishing. Two minutes from Canary Wharf station, inside Crossrail Place - the same building the roof garden sits on top of.

activities.name: Columbia Road Flower Market
activities.style: Sunday flower market
activities.whyGo: A Victorian street packed shoulder to shoulder with flower sellers shouting prices down, plus the independent shops behind them that only open when the market does.
activities.opNote: SUNDAYS ONLY, roughly 8am to 3pm. It does not exist the rest of the week. Go before 10am for room to move or after 2pm for the closing-down prices.

activities.name: Dennis Severs' House
activities.style: Silent candlelit house
activities.whyGo: A Georgian house arranged as though the family has just left the room - half-eaten food, unmade beds, candles burning. You walk it in complete silence and nothing is explained.
activities.opNote: SILENCE IS ENFORCED and that is the point. Booked in advance, limited numbers, candlelit evening slots are the ones worth having. Not suitable for young children.

activities.name: Museum of the Home
activities.style: Rooms through the centuries
activities.whyGo: A row of eighteenth-century almshouses laid out as domestic rooms from 1600 to now, with period gardens behind - free, and almost never busy.
activities.opNote: Free entry. Closed Mondays. The gardens are worth as much time as the rooms and are seasonal.

activities.name: Ballie Ballerson
activities.style: Ball pit cocktail bar
activities.whyGo: A million balls in two lit pits with a cocktail bar attached - exactly as silly as it sounds, and it has outlasted every venue that copied it.
activities.opNote: OVER 18 ONLY - it reads as a children's venue and is not. Sessions are booked by the hour.

activities.name: Hijingo
activities.style: Immersive bingo
activities.whyGo: Bingo rebuilt as a light show, with a Blade Runner-ish set, a live host and electronic tickets that mark themselves.
activities.opNote: Over 18. Booked by the session, and the sessions have fixed start times - arriving late means missing a game.

activities.name: Junkyard Golf Club
activities.style: Themed crazy golf
activities.whyGo: Nine holes threaded through scrap-built neon mazes, with a cocktail in your other hand.
activities.opNote: Over 18 after a certain hour - CHECK THE CUTOFF, it varies by site and day.

activities.name: Bounce
activities.style: Ping pong bar
activities.whyGo: Ping pong tables with pizza and a bar - the original of the format in London, and still the one that works for a group who cannot agree.
activities.opNote: Tables booked by the hour. Age policy tightens in the evening - VERIFY THE CUTOFF.

activities.name: Village Underground
activities.style: Warehouse music venue
activities.whyGo: A Victorian warehouse with tube carriages and a shipping container parked on the roof as studios - one of the last big rooms in Shoreditch that is still about the music.
activities.opNote: Gig-dependent - there is nothing to visit when nothing is on. CHECK THE LISTING BEFORE TRAVELLING.

activities.name: Rough Trade East
activities.style: Record shop and gig space
activities.whyGo: A large record shop in the Truman Brewery with a stage at the back - in-store gigs are free with an album purchase and are often bands that will not play a room this size again.
activities.opNote: Free to browse. In-store gigs are ticketed by album purchase and sell out - check the listings.

activities.name: Rich Mix
activities.style: Independent arts centre
activities.whyGo: A charity-run arts centre with three screens showing what the multiplexes will not, plus live comedy and music in the same building.
activities.opNote: Included under the cinema rule because it is an INDEPENDENT arts centre rather than a chain multiplex - the room and the programme are the reason to go.

activities.name: Shoreditch Street Art
activities.style: Self-guided or guided murals
activities.duration: An hour self-guided, three on a tour
activities.whyGo: The walls around Brick Lane, Redchurch Street and Hanbury Street change constantly - what you photograph this month will be painted over next.
activities.opNote: Free to walk. Guided tours run about two and three-quarter hours and are worth it only if you want the context - the walls are open to everyone.

activities.name: Camden Market
activities.style: Market, street food and shopping
activities.whyGo: Camden Lock, the Stables and Hawley Wharf run together into the best-known collection of street vendors in Britain - vintage, records, band merch and several hundred food stalls.
activities.opNote: Free to walk in and the busiest thing in Camden. Weekends are shoulder-to-shoulder by midday; a weekday morning is a genuinely different experience.

activities.name: Plonk Crazy Golf Camden
activities.style: Nine-hole course in a railway arch
activities.address: Unit 63, The Stables Market, 842 Chalk Farm Road
activities.whyGo: Nine holes crammed into a railway arch in the Stables Market, played under colour-changing lights with the music up.
activities.opNote: Children from about age 7, but UNDER-18s ONLY BEFORE 5PM ON WEEKDAYS - so an after-school or weekend family visit does not work. Book for Saturdays.

activities.name: Mission: Breakout
activities.style: Escape rooms in a disused Tube station
activities.whyGo: Built inside the abandoned South Kentish Town Underground station - the room is a real disused Tube station, which no amount of set dressing anywhere else can match.
activities.opNote: The venue is the attraction. Book ahead; the station rooms sell out well before the ordinary ones.

activities.name: The Roundhouse
activities.style: Live music in a Victorian engine shed
activities.whyGo: A circular Victorian railway turning shed turned concert hall, and a charity that puts a serious amount of its programme into work with young people.
activities.opNote: The round room is the reason to pick a gig here over anywhere else in London. Standing capacity, so check whether a seated ticket exists if that matters.

activities.name: KOKO
activities.style: Gigs and club nights in a former theatre
activities.whyGo: A gilded Victorian theatre with tiered balconies, reopened after a fire and a long restoration - one of the few London venues where the room outshines most of the bills.
activities.opNote: Club nights are over-18. The upper balconies give a far better view than the floor and people routinely miss that they can go up.

activities.name: Jazz Cafe
activities.style: Nightly live music, jazz to soul and hip hop
activities.whyGo: Live acts every night of the week across a far wider range than the name suggests, with a balcony you can book a table on and eat while you watch.
activities.opNote: The balcony dinner tables are the thing worth knowing - book those rather than standing downstairs if you want to sit.

activities.name: Regent's Canal Boat to Little Venice
activities.style: Narrowboat trip along the canal
activities.whyGo: The canal runs from Camden Lock past the edge of Regent's Park and London Zoo to Little Venice, which is a much better way to cover that ground than the road above it.
activities.opNote: Runs in both directions and you can go one way and walk back in about an hour. Reduced or suspended service in winter - check before relying on it.

activities.name: Primrose Hill
activities.style: Hilltop park with a protected view
activities.whyGo: A ten-minute walk from Camden Market to one of London's legally protected views - the whole central skyline laid out from a grass slope, for nothing.
activities.opNote: Free and open all the time. The summit path is a genuine climb; the north-eastern approach from Regent's Park Road is the gentler one.

activities.name: ZSL London Zoo
activities.style: The world's oldest scientific zoo
activities.whyGo: Opened in 1828 as the world's first scientific zoo, and the listed Victorian and modernist buildings are as much of the visit as the animals.
activities.opNote: Book online in advance - walk-up is materially more expensive. Allow half a day; people routinely underestimate the site.

activities.name: Royal Observatory Greenwich
activities.style: The Prime Meridian and the history of timekeeping
activities.whyGo: Longitude zero, Harrison's sea clocks, and the courtyard line where the eastern and western hemispheres meet - the reason the world's clocks are set the way they are.
activities.opNote: Ticketed, and it sits at the top of a steep hill in Greenwich Park. The view back over the Old Royal Naval College to Canary Wharf is free and does not need a ticket.

activities.name: Peter Harrison Planetarium
activities.style: London's only planetarium
activities.whyGo: The only planetarium in London, in a tilted bronze cone on the Observatory site, with shows narrated live by an astronomer rather than pre-recorded.
activities.opNote: Separate timed ticket from the Observatory and shows sell out. Book the show first and plan the rest of the hill around it.

activities.name: Cutty Sark
activities.style: Tea clipper you can walk underneath
activities.whyGo: The last surviving tea clipper, raised three metres so you can stand underneath the hull and look up at the lines that made her the fastest ship of her day.
activities.opNote: The under-hull space is free to walk through as a cafe - you do not need a ticket for that part, which almost nobody realises.

activities.name: National Maritime Museum
activities.style: The world's largest maritime museum
activities.whyGo: Free, enormous, and holds Nelson's Trafalgar coat with the bullet hole still in the shoulder.
activities.opNote: Permanent galleries are free; the temporary exhibitions are ticketed. The children's galleries are among the best free ones in London.

activities.name: Greenwich Market
activities.style: Covered market inside a World Heritage site
activities.whyGo: Trading since 1737 and the only London market inside a World Heritage site - designer-makers, antiques and a strong street food run under one roof.
activities.opNote: Covered, so it works in rain when the rest of Greenwich does not. Different traders on different days: antiques and collectables do not run every day.

activities.name: Greenwich Park
activities.style: Royal park with a deer enclosure and boating lake
activities.whyGo: 183 acres holding a deer enclosure, a boating pond, a rose garden and London's longest herbaceous border, with the best free view in south London at the top.
activities.opNote: Free and open daily. The hill is steep - the path up from the Maritime Museum side is the gentlest way to the Observatory.

activities.name: Greenwich Foot Tunnel
activities.style: Victorian tunnel under the Thames
activities.whyGo: Walk under the Thames through a tiled Victorian tunnel and come up on the Isle of Dogs with the whole Greenwich waterfront laid out behind you.
activities.opNote: Free, open 24 hours, and step-free by lift - though the lifts do fail and the stairs are a long spiral. The view back from Island Gardens is the real reward.

activities.name: IFS Cloud Cable Car
activities.style: Cable car across the Thames
activities.whyGo: The only cable car crossing of the Thames, running from the Peninsula to the Royal Docks at a height that puts Canary Wharf below eye level.
activities.opNote: Takes contactless and is cheaper with an Oyster. Closes in high wind, so it is not something to build a plan around.

activities.name: Up at The O2
activities.style: Guided climb over the roof of The O2
activities.whyGo: A harnessed walk over the tented roof of The O2 to a viewing platform 52 metres up, looking back along the river to Canary Wharf and the City.
activities.opNote: Minimum age and a minimum height apply and it is not step-free. Sunset slots cost more and sell out first. Runs in rain, cancels in high wind.

activities.name: TOCA Social
activities.style: Interactive football booths with food and drink
activities.whyGo: Private booths where a screen and a ball-feeder turn football into a target game - it works whether or not anyone in the group can actually play.
activities.opNote: Booked by the box rather than per person, so a small group pays the same as a large one. Under-18s must be out by early evening on most nights.

activities.name: CrazyPutt Adventure Golf
activities.style: 18 holes modelled on famous courses
activities.whyGo: Eighteen holes done in deliberately old-fashioned 1980s crazy golf style, with holes modelled on the Belfry, Wentworth, Augusta and St Andrews.
activities.opNote: Outdoor and a few hundred metres from North Greenwich station. The opposite of the polished bar-and-golf venues in the centre, and cheaper for it.

activities.name: Greenwich Peninsula Ecology Park
activities.style: Freshwater wetland reserve
activities.whyGo: Four acres of wetland, marsh and woodland hidden behind the Peninsula's towers, with hides, a lake and a genuinely surprising amount of birdlife.
activities.opNote: Free, and closed on Mondays and Tuesdays - the single most common reason people find the gate shut. Step-free boardwalks throughout.

activities.name: London Eye
activities.style: Observation wheel on the Thames
activities.whyGo: One full rotation at 135 metres over the river, and still the clearest way to work out how London fits together on a first visit.
activities.opNote: Book a timed slot online - walk-up costs more and the queue is the whole experience otherwise. Capsules are shared unless you pay for a private one.

activities.name: SEA LIFE London Aquarium
activities.style: Aquarium in the basement of County Hall
activities.whyGo: A walk-through shark tunnel and a rockhopper penguin colony in the basement of County Hall, which is a strange and good place for an aquarium to be.
activities.opNote: Timed entry and much cheaper booked online. Combined tickets with the London Eye next door are usually better value than two separate ones.

activities.name: Southbank Centre
activities.style: Arts centre with free foyers and exhibitions
activities.whyGo: Europe's largest arts centre, and the foyers, outdoor artworks and a good share of the exhibitions cost nothing at all to walk into.
activities.opNote: The free programme is the point and it is genuinely substantial. The Royal Festival Hall foyer is open to anyone to sit and work in, with no purchase expected.

activities.name: Hayward Gallery
activities.style: Brutalist contemporary art gallery
activities.whyGo: A 1968 Brutalist box with pyramid rooflights, running two or three large contemporary shows a year that tend to be the immersive, walk-into-them kind.
activities.opNote: Ticketed and separate from the free Southbank Centre programme. The upper sculpture terraces reopened after restoration and are part of the ticket.

activities.name: BFI IMAX
activities.style: The largest cinema screen in the UK
activities.whyGo: The biggest screen in the country, in a glass drum marooned in the middle of a Waterloo roundabout - the room is emphatically the reason to go.
activities.opNote: Meets the cinema rule on this tab: it is here because of the screen, not because it shows films. Book central rows well back; the front is too close.

activities.name: BFI Southbank
activities.style: Repertory and archive cinema
activities.whyGo: Four screens of archive prints, restorations and seasons that no multiplex would touch, plus the free Mediatheque where you can watch the national archive on your own.
activities.opNote: The Mediatheque is FREE and bookable by the hour, and almost nobody outside film circles knows it exists. Meets the cinema rule as an independent repertory house.

activities.name: Undercroft Skate Space
activities.style: The world's oldest continually used skate spot
activities.whyGo: Skated continuously since 1973 and defended from redevelopment by a campaign that won - the oldest surviving skate spot on earth, still in daily use.
activities.opNote: Free to skate and free to watch, and watching is what most people do. Do not walk through the middle of it - stand at the edges.

activities.name: South Bank Book Market
activities.style: Second-hand book stalls under Waterloo Bridge
activities.whyGo: Eight stalls of second-hand books, maps and prints running under Waterloo Bridge for forty years, with traders who have been there since the 1980s.
activities.opNote: Sheltered by the bridge, so it runs in rain. Open daily but the stalls that turn up vary - the antiquarian and print sellers are not there every day.

activities.name: Coal Drops Yard
activities.style: Shopping and eating in Victorian coal sheds
activities.whyGo: Two Victorian coal drops joined by a kissing roof by Thomas Heatherwick, holding fifty-odd shops, a cinema and some of the better bars in this part of London.
activities.opNote: Traffic-free and covered in parts. Free to walk through, and the canal-side steps below it are where people actually sit.

activities.name: Granary Square Fountains
activities.style: Choreographed fountains in a canal-side square
activities.duration: As long as the children last
activities.whyGo: More than a thousand individually controlled jets in the open square by the canal, lit at night and free to run straight through in summer.
activities.opNote: Free, and the single best thing in London for small children on a hot day. Bring a towel and a change of clothes - they will get soaked.

activities.name: Word on the Water
activities.style: Bookshop on a 1920s Dutch barge
activities.whyGo: A floating second-hand bookshop on an old Dutch barge moored on the towpath, with a wood burner inside and live jazz on the roof in decent weather.
activities.opNote: Free to browse and step aboard, but it is a barge - narrow, stepped and not accessible. The roof gigs are unannounced and weather-dependent.

activities.name: Camley Street Natural Park
activities.style: Two-acre nature reserve on the canal
activities.whyGo: Wetland, meadow and woodland on a two-acre strip of former coal yard beside the canal, run by the London Wildlife Trust three minutes from a mainline terminus.
activities.opNote: Free. The contrast with St Pancras a few hundred metres away is the whole reason to go. There is a cafe in the visitor centre.

activities.name: Everyman Screen on the Canal
activities.style: Free outdoor cinema on the towpath
activities.whyGo: Films projected beside the canal in summer, watched from the towpath steps, for nothing - the rare outdoor screen that has not been turned into a ticketed event.
activities.opNote: Summer only and free, but seats are released in advance and go quickly. Meets the cinema rule as an outdoor screen rather than a multiplex.

activities.name: The British Library Treasures Gallery
activities.style: Free gallery of the library's greatest holdings
activities.whyGo: Magna Carta, Leonardo's notebook, Handel's Messiah in his own hand and Beatles lyrics on scrap paper, in one free room most people walk past on the way to a train.
activities.opNote: Free and needs no booking. Ten minutes from the Eurostar gate, which makes it the best possible way to spend a delayed departure.

activities.name: Lewis Cubitt Park
activities.style: Pocket park with a sand-pit playground
activities.whyGo: A landscaped lawn and a proper playground with a sand pit at the top of Coal Drops Yard - the place families end up when the fountains get too much.
activities.opNote: Free and quiet compared with Granary Square. Free PlayPod lockers nearby lend out table tennis bats and chess sets.

activities.name: The Painted Hall
activities.style: Baroque ceiling painting at the Old Royal Naval College
activities.address: Old Royal Naval College, King William Walk
activities.whyGo: Forty thousand square feet of baroque painting that took James Thornhill nineteen years, restored to the point where you are handed a mirror to look up without breaking your neck.
activities.opNote: NOT free, whatever the listicles say - about £19, though under-16s go free and First Sundays are £5. The ticket converts to an annual pass at no extra cost.

activities.name: Covent Garden Street Performers
activities.style: Auditioned street performance in the Piazza
activities.whyGo: Jugglers, opera singers, escapologists and contortionists working the Piazza and the Market Building - and unusually for street performance, every act has passed an audition to be there.
activities.opNote: Free, though the hat comes round and the acts earn nothing otherwise. The pitch in front of St Paul's Church takes the big physical acts; the Market Building takes the classical musicians.

activities.name: London Transport Museum
activities.style: Tube, bus and poster history in a Victorian market hall
activities.whyGo: Real Tube carriages and horse buses you can climb into, plus the poster and Johnston-typeface archive that explains why London's transport looks the way it does.
activities.opNote: The ticket lasts a whole year, which almost nobody realises. Children go free with a paying adult, and the Friday Lates are adults-only.

activities.name: Seven Dials Market
activities.style: Food hall in a former banana warehouse
activities.whyGo: Two floors of independent food traders in a 1920s banana-ripening warehouse, with a stage for live music and a bookshop tucked in among the counters.
activities.opNote: Free to walk into and no booking. The cheese conveyor belt downstairs is the thing people queue for; the upstairs tables are quieter.

activities.name: Bat & Ball Covent Garden
activities.style: Ping pong, pool and interactive darts
activities.whyGo: Ping pong, pool and interactive darts under one roof, which makes it the easy answer for a group that cannot agree on one game.
activities.opNote: Family-friendly in the day and over-18 in the evening - check the switchover time before bringing children after work.

activities.name: Royal Opera House Terrace
activities.style: Free terrace over the Piazza
activities.whyGo: The opera house's terrace bar is open to anyone during opening hours, with the best elevated view over the Piazza and Market Building in Covent Garden - and no ticket needed.
activities.opNote: You do NOT need a performance ticket to go up. Free to enter, and you are under no obligation to buy, though the bar is the point of the room.

activities.name: St Paul's, the Actors' Church
activities.style: Inigo Jones church and theatrical memorials
activities.whyGo: Inigo Jones's 1633 church, walled with memorials to actors from Ellen Terry to Charlie Chaplin, and with a quiet garden behind that most of the Piazza crowd never finds.
activities.opNote: Free and usually open in the day. The garden entrance is on Bedford Street - the portico facing the Piazza is famously a false front and not a way in.

activities.name: Neal's Yard
activities.style: Painted courtyard off Seven Dials
activities.whyGo: A tiny courtyard off Seven Dials painted in every colour and hung with plants - the most photographed twenty square metres in Covent Garden.
activities.opNote: Free, and small enough that it is genuinely crowded from mid-morning. Early is the only way to see it without a queue for the photograph.

activities.name: Ronnie Scott's
activities.style: The jazz club, since 1959
activities.whyGo: Open since 1959 and still the most famous jazz room in the world, with table service, low ceilings and a stage close enough to see the fingering.
activities.opNote: Book a table rather than a bar ticket if you want to see the stage. The Late Late Show after the main set is cheaper and much less formal.

activities.name: The Photographers' Gallery
activities.style: The UK's first gallery for photography
activities.whyGo: The first public gallery in the country devoted to photography, on a back street off Oxford Street, with a bookshop and print sales worth the trip on their own.
activities.opNote: Free entry before noon on weekdays, ticketed after. Easy to miss - it is down a side street behind the Oxford Street crowds.

activities.name: House Party
activities.style: Seven floors laid out as a house
activities.whyGo: Seven storeys done out as rooms of a house - DJ sets in the kitchen, karaoke in the parents' bedroom, beer pong on the roof - with actors working the floors in character.
activities.opNote: Over-18 throughout. Co-founded by Stormzy and open since 2024; it is a bar and club rather than a bookable game, so there is nothing to reserve beyond a table.

activities.name: The Crystal Maze LIVE Experience
activities.style: Playable version of the TV show
activities.whyGo: Aztec, Medieval, Industrial and Futuristic zones played against the clock with a live Maze Master, ending in the Crystal Dome with the gold tickets whipping round.
activities.opNote: Teams are combined with strangers unless you book the whole slot. VERIFIED at 22-32 Shaftesbury Avenue - it moved from its original Angel site and older guides still send people north.

activities.name: Karaoke Box Soho
activities.style: Japanese-style private karaoke rooms
activities.whyGo: Proper Japanese-format private rooms rather than a stage in a pub - your group, your booth, a door that shuts, and a sake list.
activities.opNote: Booked by the room by the hour, so the cost per head falls sharply with numbers. Open very late at weekends.

activities.name: Lucky Voice Soho
activities.style: Private booths with a self-service song list
activities.whyGo: The original of the London private-booth karaoke format, with a button on the wall that summons drinks so nobody has to leave mid-song.
activities.opNote: Over-18 only, unlike some of the newer competition. Book the room, not the person - a half-full booth costs the same as a packed one.

activities.name: Soho Square
activities.style: Garden square with a mock-Tudor hut
activities.whyGo: The one patch of grass in Soho, with a half-timbered garden hut in the middle that hides the entrance to an electricity substation.
activities.opNote: Free and locked overnight. Full to bursting on the first warm day of the year and half empty for most of the rest.

activities.name: Carnaby Street
activities.style: Pedestrianised independent shopping street
activities.whyGo: The street the Sixties happened on, now thirteen pedestrianised lanes of independents and the best Christmas lights in central London.
activities.opNote: Free to walk. Kingly Court off the middle of it is the part worth finding - three tiers of small restaurants around an open courtyard.

activities.name: Sky Garden
activities.style: London's highest public garden
activities.whyGo: Three storeys of planted terraces under a glass shell on top of the Walkie-Talkie, with a 360-degree view over the City - and it costs nothing.
activities.opNote: FREE but the timed tickets are released in batches and go within minutes. Booking a table at one of the bars gets you in without the ticket lottery.

activities.name: The Garden at 120
activities.style: Free rooftop garden, no booking
activities.whyGo: Fifteen storeys up with a 360-degree view, a water rill and wisteria walkways - and unlike Sky Garden across the road, you can simply walk in.
activities.opNote: Free and NO BOOKING needed for groups under twelve, which is the single best thing about it. Outdoor, so it closes in bad weather.

activities.name: The Lookout at 8 Bishopsgate
activities.style: Free viewing gallery on the 50th floor
activities.whyGo: The 50th floor, a 240-degree sweep across the City, and the newest of London's free high viewpoints - which means it is still the least crowded of them.
activities.opNote: Free, but tickets are released fortnightly on a Monday and go quickly. Same-day walk-ins are let in only if there is capacity.

activities.name: Barbican Conservatory
activities.style: Tropical glasshouse inside a Brutalist arts centre
activities.whyGo: Over 1,500 species of tropical plants and a pond of koi and terrapins, grown inside the concrete fly tower of a Brutalist theatre - the second largest conservatory in London and by far the strangest.
activities.opNote: Free on selected days only and it is not open daily - check before travelling, which is the most common mistake here. Book the free slot online.

activities.name: St Dunstan in the East
activities.style: Bombed church ruin turned public garden
activities.whyGo: A Wren church gutted in the Blitz and left as a shell, now filled with climbing plants and trees growing up through the empty windows.
activities.opNote: Free and open in daylight hours. Very small and very popular for photographs - go early or at lunchtime on a weekend when the City empties.

activities.name: Postman's Park
activities.style: Victorian memorial to ordinary heroism
activities.whyGo: A wall of hand-painted ceramic tablets, each recording an ordinary person who died saving someone else - the quietest and most affecting thing in the Square Mile.
activities.opNote: Free, open in daylight, and takes twenty minutes. Read the tablets rather than photographing them; that is the whole point of the place.

activities.name: Bank of England Museum
activities.style: Free museum inside the Bank
activities.whyGo: Free, inside the Bank itself, and it lets you lift a real gold bar out of a perspex case - which is the bit everyone remembers.
activities.opNote: Free and no booking. Weekdays only - it is shut at weekends and on bank holidays, which catches out most weekend visitors.

activities.name: London's Roman Amphitheatre
activities.style: Roman ruins under the Guildhall Art Gallery
activities.whyGo: The remains of Londinium's amphitheatre in the basement of the Guildhall Art Gallery, with the missing seating drawn back in as green light on the walls.
activities.opNote: Free, and included with the free Guildhall Art Gallery above it. The black ring in the paving of Guildhall Yard outside traces its full size.

activities.name: Leadenhall Market
activities.style: Victorian covered market arcade
activities.whyGo: An 1881 covered market in cream, maroon and green wrought iron, standing where the Roman forum was, and standing in for Diagon Alley on film.
activities.opNote: Free to walk through and covered. Dead at weekends - the shops and bars serve City workers, so Saturday gets you the architecture and nothing else.

activities.name: Churchill War Rooms
activities.style: The wartime bunker, left as it was
activities.whyGo: The underground rooms the war was run from, shut up in 1945 and largely untouched - the Map Room still has the pins in it from the day the lights went out.
activities.opNote: Timed tickets and it sells out days ahead in summer. Allow two hours; the audio guide is included and worth using.

activities.name: Westminster Abbey
activities.style: Coronation church and royal burial site
activities.whyGo: Every coronation since 1066, seventeen monarchs buried in it, and Poets' Corner - plus the Queen's Diamond Jubilee Galleries up in the medieval triforium.
activities.opNote: Ticketed for sightseeing, but FREE if you attend a service - Evensong most weekdays, no ticket, and you sit in the quire. Closed to sightseers on Sundays.

activities.name: The Supreme Court
activities.style: Sit in on a live case, for free
activities.whyGo: You can walk in off Parliament Square and sit at the back of the highest court in the land while it hears a real case, for nothing and without booking.
activities.opNote: Free, no booking, and almost nobody does it. Court sits weekday mornings in term; the exhibition in the basement is open whether or not a case is running.

activities.name: St James's Park
activities.style: The oldest royal park, with pelicans
activities.whyGo: A resident pelican colony first given to Charles II by a Russian ambassador, and the view from the Blue Bridge back to Buckingham Palace and forward to Whitehall.
activities.opNote: Free. The pelicans are fed daily in the afternoon near Duck Island, which is the one thing worth timing a visit around.

activities.name: Changing the Guard
activities.style: Free ceremonial handover at Buckingham Palace
activities.whyGo: Guards in bearskins and a full regimental band handing over the palace, free to watch, and one of the few genuinely free set-piece spectacles in London.
activities.opNote: Does not run daily and is cancelled in heavy rain - check the schedule the same morning. The railings are five deep by the start; the Victoria Memorial steps and the Mall give a better view.

activities.name: Tate Britain
activities.style: Five centuries of British art, free
activities.whyGo: The national collection of British art from 1500 on, free, and holding the Turner bequest - which is the largest collection of one artist's work anywhere in Britain.
activities.opNote: Permanent collection free, exhibitions ticketed. The Tate Boat runs from here to Tate Modern in about fifteen minutes and is far better than the Tube.

activities.name: Westminster Cathedral Tower
activities.style: Lift up a Byzantine campanile
activities.whyGo: A lift 64 metres up the campanile of a striped Byzantine cathedral, with a view over Westminster that hardly anyone queues for - and the cathedral itself is free.
activities.opNote: The cathedral is free; the tower is a small charge and the lift means no stairs. Half-finished blackened brick interior above the marble is deliberate - the money ran out.

activities.name: Royal Academy of Arts
activities.style: Exhibitions at Burlington House
activities.whyGo: Britain's first art school, founded 1768 and still artist-run, putting on the biggest exhibitions in London plus the Summer Exhibition, which anyone at all can submit to.
activities.opNote: The courtyard, the Collection Gallery and the Weston Studio are FREE - you only pay for the temporary shows. Most visitors do not realise there is anything free here at all.

activities.name: Handel Hendrix House
activities.style: Two musicians' homes, two centuries apart
activities.whyGo: Handel lived at 25 Brook Street from 1723 until he died there in 1759; Jimi Hendrix lived in the upstairs flat next door in 1968. Both rooms are restored and you walk between them.
activities.opNote: A Georgian townhouse over several floors with no lift, so it is not step-free. Small - an hour is genuinely enough.

activities.name: The Faraday Museum
activities.style: Free science museum at the Royal Institution
activities.whyGo: Faraday's actual magnetic laboratory, preserved in the basement of the Royal Institution, where the electric motor and the transformer were worked out. Ten elements were first isolated in this building.
activities.opNote: Free and one of the very few free things in Mayfair. Weekdays only in practice - check before a weekend trip.

activities.name: Cork Street Galleries
activities.style: Commercial art dealers, free to walk into
activities.whyGo: A single street of dealers - Waddington Custot, Hamiltons, Sims Reed - with museum-standard work on the walls, and every one of them free to walk into.
activities.opNote: They are shops, not museums, and nobody will mind you looking. Closed Sundays and often Mondays. Gagosian, Hauser & Wirth and White Cube are a few streets away on the same terms.

activities.name: Brown Hart Gardens
activities.style: Raised garden on an electricity substation
activities.whyGo: A raised stone terrace built on the roof of a working Edwardian electricity substation, two minutes off Oxford Street and almost always empty.
activities.opNote: Free and open daily. Steps up on both sides, though there is a lift. There is a cafe on the deck if you want a reason to sit.

activities.name: Mount Street Gardens
activities.style: Sheltered garden with a famous microclimate
activities.whyGo: A walled garden so sheltered that Australian mimosa and Canary Island palms survive in it, hidden behind Mount Street and lined with benches donated by American visitors.
activities.opNote: Free, and the quietest place to sit in Mayfair. Read the bench plaques - most were given by Americans who loved the garden, and they are the best thing in it.

activities.name: Shepherd Market
activities.style: Pedestrian village of lanes and pubs
activities.whyGo: A pocket of narrow pedestrian lanes, small shops and old pubs left over from the eighteenth-century May Fair itself - the least Mayfair-looking corner of Mayfair.
activities.opNote: Free to wander and the pub tables spill into the lanes in summer. Two minutes from Green Park station and most people walk straight past the entrance.

activities.name: Portobello Road Market
activities.style: The UK's largest antiques market
activities.whyGo: Two miles of stalls running from antiques at the Notting Hill end through fruit and veg to vintage under the Westway - the largest antiques market in Britain.
activities.opNote: SATURDAY is the antiques day and the only day the full market runs; the rest of the week is a fraction of it. Go before ten or accept you will be shuffling.

activities.name: Electric Cinema
activities.style: 1910 cinema with armchairs and beds
activities.whyGo: One of the oldest working cinemas in Britain, open since 1910, with 83 leather armchairs, footstools, and six double beds in the front row.
activities.opNote: The room is entirely the point - this is the venue the cinema rule on this tab was written around. Book the beds or the back-row sofas well ahead; in-seat service runs throughout.

activities.name: Museum of Brands
activities.style: A time tunnel of packaging and advertising
activities.whyGo: A Time Tunnel of twelve thousand everyday objects - biscuit tins, cereal boxes, magazines - running from the Victorians to now. Everyone finds their own childhood in it.
activities.opNote: Small, indoor and genuinely different from anything else in west London. There is a garden and a cafe at the back that you do not need a ticket for.

activities.name: Biscuiteers Icing Cafe
activities.style: Biscuit decorating classes
activities.whyGo: A two-hour icing class in a shop got up like a sweet shop, where you decorate biscuits badly, drink something, and take the results home in a box.
activities.opNote: Booked classes rather than walk-in, and they run for adults as well as children - the adult evening ones come with a drink.

activities.name: Golborne Road
activities.style: Vintage, Moroccan and Portuguese end of Portobello
activities.whyGo: The far end past the Westway, where the antiques give way to midcentury furniture, Moroccan groceries and Portuguese cafes - and the prices drop with the tourist numbers.
activities.opNote: Friday and Saturday for the stalls. Ten minutes further than most Portobello visitors walk, which is exactly why it is worth doing.

activities.name: Natural History Museum
activities.style: Free natural history in a cathedral of a building
activities.whyGo: Eighty million specimens behind a terracotta Romanesque front, with a blue whale skeleton diving through Hintze Hall and the best dinosaur collection in the country.
activities.opNote: Free but book a timed slot in school holidays or expect a long queue on Cromwell Road. The Exhibition Road entrance is almost always shorter.

activities.name: Science Museum
activities.style: Free, and hands-on from the second floor up
activities.whyGo: Stephenson's Rocket, the Apollo 10 command module and a working section of Babbage's difference engine, plus Wonderlab upstairs where children are meant to touch everything.
activities.opNote: The museum is free; Wonderlab and the IMAX are ticketed and worth it with children. Adults-only Lates on the last Wednesday of the month.

activities.name: Victoria and Albert Museum
activities.style: The world's largest museum of decorative arts
activities.whyGo: Raphael cartoons, the Cast Courts with a full-size Trajan's Column in two halves, and the oldest museum restaurant in the world - all free.
activities.opNote: Free, no booking, and far quieter than the two museums either side of it. The John Madejski Garden in the middle has a paddling pool in summer and needs no ticket.

activities.name: Royal Albert Hall Tour
activities.style: Guided tour of the auditorium and boxes
activities.whyGo: Gets you into the auditorium, the Royal Retiring Room and the grand tier boxes on a day with no concert - and explains the mushroom-shaped acoustic diffusers hanging from the roof.
activities.opNote: Runs most days but cancels when the hall is in use, so check the same week. The tour is the only way in without a ticket to something.

activities.name: Natural History Museum Ice Rink
activities.style: Outdoor rink in front of the museum
activities.whyGo: Skating in the museum's front garden under the terracotta facade and a lit tree - the best-looking of London's winter rinks by a distance.
activities.opNote: Late October to January only, and sessions sell out weeks ahead at weekends. Weekday mornings are the quiet slots.

activities.name: Kensington Palace
activities.style: State apartments and royal dress collection
activities.whyGo: Where Victoria was born and grew up, with the King's and Queen's State Apartments and a dress collection that runs from court mantuas to Diana's wardrobe.
activities.opNote: Ticketed, but the Sunken Garden outside is free and is the bit most people photograph. Historic Royal Palaces membership pays for itself in two visits.

activities.name: Kyoto Garden, Holland Park
activities.style: Japanese garden with a waterfall and koi
activities.whyGo: A tiered Japanese garden given by Kyoto in 1991, with a waterfall, a koi pond and peacocks that wander in from the rest of Holland Park.
activities.opNote: Free, no ticket, open from 7.30am until half an hour before dusk. Tiny and very popular - early morning is the only time it is quiet.

activities.name: Leighton House
activities.style: A Victorian painter's Arab Hall
activities.whyGo: Frederic Leighton built himself a house around an Arab Hall lined with Iznik tiles, a gilded dome and a fountain in the floor. There is nothing else like it in London.
activities.opNote: Small, ticketed and closed on Tuesdays. The Arab Hall is the whole reason to come and it is the first room you reach.

activities.name: The Design Museum
activities.style: Design under a hyperbolic paraboloid roof
activities.whyGo: The former Commonwealth Institute, gutted and rebuilt under its listed swooping concrete roof, with a permanent design collection that costs nothing.
activities.opNote: The permanent Designer Maker User gallery is FREE; the temporary exhibitions are ticketed. Walk into the atrium just to look up at the roof, even if you do nothing else.

activities.name: Serpentine Galleries
activities.style: Two free contemporary galleries in a park
activities.whyGo: Two free contemporary art galleries five minutes apart across the Serpentine bridge, plus the summer Pavilion - a new one commissioned from a different architect every year.
activities.opNote: Free, Tuesday to Sunday. The Pavilion stands from roughly June to October and is the reason to come in summer; there is nothing to see of it the rest of the year.

activities.name: Boating on the Serpentine
activities.style: Rowing boats and pedalos on the lake
activities.whyGo: Rowing boats and pedalos on the lake in the middle of Hyde Park, hired by the half hour, with the Serpentine bar at the end of it.
activities.opNote: Daily from late March to October, then weekends only and weather-dependent through winter. Boats take four adults and are hired per boat, not per head.

activities.name: Diana Memorial Playground
activities.style: Pirate-ship playground in Kensington Gardens
activities.whyGo: A wooden pirate ship in a sand pit, a teepee camp and a musical garden, built where Barrie set Peter Pan - and free.
activities.opNote: Free. ADULTS ARE ONLY ADMITTED WITH A CHILD, which is the rule people most often arrive not knowing. Gets very busy after school and in holidays.

activities.name: The British Museum
activities.style: Eight million objects, free
activities.whyGo: The Rosetta Stone, the Parthenon sculptures and the Sutton Hoo helmet under Foster's glass-roofed Great Court - and none of it costs anything.
activities.opNote: Free but book a slot at busy times. It is far too big for one visit - pick three galleries and accept you will not see the rest. Fridays are open late.

activities.name: Charles Dickens Museum
activities.style: The only surviving Dickens house in London
activities.whyGo: The Georgian terrace where Dickens wrote Oliver Twist and Nicholas Nickleby, laid out as he lived in it, down to the desk.
activities.opNote: A townhouse over four floors with no lift. Small enough for an hour, and the garden cafe is open without a ticket.

activities.name: The Foundling Museum
activities.style: Britain's first children's charity, and its art collection
activities.whyGo: The story of the Foundling Hospital, founded 1739, told partly through the scraps of fabric mothers left as tokens so they could one day identify the child they gave up.
activities.opNote: The tokens are the reason to come and they are quietly devastating. Hogarth and Handel both backed the hospital, so the art and music collections are far better than the size suggests.

activities.name: Wellcome Collection
activities.style: Free museum about medicine and being human
activities.whyGo: Free, genuinely strange, and built around Henry Wellcome's collection of medical objects - which runs from Napoleon's toothbrush to a Peruvian mummy.
activities.opNote: Free and needs no booking. The Reading Room upstairs is open to anyone to sit in, and almost nobody goes up.

activities.name: Grant Museum of Zoology
activities.style: A Victorian teaching collection in jars
activities.whyGo: One cramped room of UCL's zoological teaching collection - 68,000 specimens including a jar packed with preserved moles and the bones of a quagga, an animal that no longer exists.
activities.opNote: Free and tiny. University hours, so it closes over the holidays when most visitors are around - check before walking over.

activities.name: Petrie Museum of Egyptian Archaeology
activities.style: 80,000 objects of everyday Egyptian life
activities.whyGo: Where the British Museum has the monuments, the Petrie has the ordinary things - the world's oldest dress, the earliest metal from Egypt, and a lot of it in the original wooden cases.
activities.opNote: Free, hidden inside a UCL building and easy to walk past. University opening hours. They hand out torches for the dim cases, which tells you the register of the place.

activities.name: The Bloomsbury Squares
activities.style: A self-guided round of the garden squares
activities.address: Russell Square, Bloomsbury Square, Gordon Square
activities.whyGo: Russell, Bedford, Gordon, Tavistock and Bloomsbury squares in one walk, with the blue plaques of the Bloomsbury Group - Woolf, Keynes, Strachey - clustered round Gordon Square.
activities.opNote: Free and takes about an hour at a slow pace. Some squares are private and locked; Russell, Gordon and Bloomsbury are all open to anyone.

activities.name: The Wallace Collection
activities.style: A private art collection left whole, free
activities.whyGo: Frans Hals's Laughing Cavalier, Fragonard's The Swing, and one of the best armour collections in Europe, in the townhouse they were assembled in - and free.
activities.opNote: Free, no booking, and consistently the least crowded major collection in central London. The glazed courtyard restaurant is one of the nicest rooms in Marylebone.

activities.name: Madame Tussauds London
activities.style: The wax museum, since 1835
activities.whyGo: Open on Marylebone Road since 1835 and still the busiest paid attraction in the area - wax figures, a Marvel section and a black-cab ride through London history.
activities.opNote: Book a timed slot online; walk-up prices are much higher and the queue is long. Peak school holidays are genuinely crowded rather than merely busy.

activities.name: The Sherlock Holmes Museum
activities.style: 221b Baker Street, furnished as the stories describe
activities.whyGo: A Georgian house done out exactly as Conan Doyle described 221b, with the study, the chemistry bench and the view over Baker Street from the first floor.
activities.opNote: Steep narrow stairs and no lift. Cash-free, ticketed at the shop next door, and the queue on the pavement is often longer than the visit.

activities.name: Regent's Park and Queen Mary's Gardens
activities.style: Royal park with London's biggest rose garden
activities.whyGo: Nearly 400 acres, with Queen Mary's Gardens holding over 12,000 roses in 85 beds - the largest rose collection in London and free to walk into.
activities.opNote: Free. The roses peak from late May to July and are worth timing a visit around; outside that window the gardens are pleasant rather than remarkable.

activities.name: Boating on Regent's Park Lake
activities.style: Rowing boats and pedalos on the boating lake
activities.whyGo: Rowing boats and pedalos on a heron-covered lake with the Nash terraces behind it, hired by the half hour, and much quieter than the Serpentine.
activities.opNote: Seasonal and weather-dependent - reduced or closed in winter. There is a separate small children's boating pond nearby, which is not the same thing.

activities.name: Daunt Books Marylebone
activities.style: Edwardian galleried bookshop arranged by country
activities.whyGo: A purpose-built Edwardian bookshop with oak galleries, a long skylight and a conservatory at the back, where the travel section is shelved by country rather than by genre.
activities.opNote: Free to walk into and the back room is the photograph everyone comes for. Genuinely a working bookshop, so browse rather than treating it as a set.

activities.name: The Fitzrovia Chapel
activities.style: Gold mosaic chapel of a demolished hospital
activities.whyGo: The last surviving fragment of the Middlesex Hospital, demolished around it. A plain brick exterior hides a ceiling of gold mosaic finished in 1929 by the architect's son.
activities.opNote: Free, no booking, donation box only. Generally open Monday to Wednesday 11am-5pm plus one Sunday a month - so the two days most visitors are free are the two it is likely shut. Check the What's On page.

activities.name: All Saints, Margaret Street
activities.style: The most decorated Victorian Gothic interior in London
activities.whyGo: William Butterfield's 1859 church, where every surface is patterned tile, marble or paint - the loudest interior in London, thirty seconds off Oxford Street.
activities.opNote: Free and usually open in the day. Almost nobody goes in despite the location, which is most of the pleasure of it.

activities.name: The Cartoon Museum
activities.style: British cartoons, caricature and comics
activities.whyGo: Three hundred years of British cartooning from Hogarth and Gillray to Beano originals, with drawing tables out so children can have a go.
activities.opNote: Open TUESDAY, WEDNESDAY, FRIDAY AND SATURDAY only, 10.30am to 5.30pm - shut Mondays, Thursdays and Sundays, which is an odd enough pattern to check before walking over.

activities.name: Fitzroy Square
activities.style: Pedestrianised Georgian square
activities.whyGo: Robert Adam frontages on two sides, fully pedestrianised, and almost always empty - Virginia Woolf and George Bernard Shaw both lived on it, at the same address.
activities.opNote: The paved square is free and open; the central garden itself is private. Five minutes from Oxford Street and silent.

activities.name: Little Venice Canal Boat to Camden
activities.style: Narrowboat along the Regent's Canal
activities.whyGo: Forty-five minutes by narrowboat from Little Venice through Maida Hill tunnel and past London Zoo to Camden Lock - the best way to see the canal there is.
activities.opNote: Several operators run it - London Waterbus, Jason's Trip, Jenny Wren. Boats are stepped and not accessible. Reduced service in winter.

activities.name: GoBoat Paddington
activities.style: Self-drive electric picnic boats
activities.whyGo: You drive it yourself. An electric boat with a table in the middle, no licence needed, and you bring your own picnic and drinks aboard.
activities.opNote: Hired by the boat rather than per head, up to eight people, so a full boat is much better value. Bring your own food and drink - that is the intended use.

activities.name: Puppet Theatre Barge
activities.style: A marionette theatre on a canal barge
activities.whyGo: A fifty-seat marionette theatre inside a converted Thames barge moored at Little Venice, running since 1982 and rocking gently while you watch.
activities.opNote: Meets the theatre rule on this tab - the barge IS the reason to go. Fifty seats, so it sells out. Not accessible: you board down steps into a hold.

activities.name: Paddington Bear Statue and Pawprint Trail
activities.style: Free self-guided family trail
activities.whyGo: The bronze Paddington on Platform 1, then a free trail of brass pawprints set into the pavements around the station and the basin.
activities.opNote: Free and self-guided, and the single best thing to do here with small children. The statue has a queue at weekends.

activities.name: Paddington Basin Moving Bridges
activities.style: Heatherwick's Rolling Bridge and the Fan Bridge
activities.whyGo: Thomas Heatherwick's Rolling Bridge curls itself into an octagon, and the Fan Bridge next to it opens like a hand of cards. Both are working footbridges and both are free to watch.
activities.opNote: They only move on a published schedule, usually once or twice a week at a set time - turning up unplanned gets you two ordinary footbridges. Check before going.

activities.name: Broadway Market
activities.style: Saturday street market by the canal
activities.whyGo: A hundred and twenty stalls of food, vintage and produce running from the canal to London Fields, with seventy independent shops behind them that trade all week.
activities.opNote: The market is SATURDAY only, 9am to 5pm - the street is worth a visit any day, the market is not. Buy lunch and eat it in London Fields at the top.

activities.name: London Fields Lido
activities.style: Heated 50-metre outdoor pool, open all year
activities.whyGo: An Olympic-length 50-metre outdoor pool, heated, and open every day of the year - swimming outside in Hackney in February is a genuinely strange pleasure.
activities.opNote: Heated year-round, which is the point. Book a lane slot; early mornings and evenings fill with regulars and it is busy on hot days.

activities.name: Victoria Park
activities.style: The People's Park, with a pagoda and a deer enclosure
activities.whyGo: Eighty-six hectares with a boating lake, a deer enclosure and a Chinese pagoda on the eastern side that most Londoners do not know is there.
activities.opNote: Free. The Sunday food market by the Grove Road gate is small and good. The park hosts big summer festivals, on which weekends much of it is fenced off.

activities.name: Hackney City Farm
activities.style: A working city farm, free to enter
activities.whyGo: Pigs, goats, donkeys and chickens on a scrap of land off Hackney Road, free to walk into, with a good cafe and a pottery in the yard.
activities.opNote: Free, donations asked. Closed Mondays. Small - an hour is plenty, and it is best combined with a walk down to the canal.

activities.name: Sutton House
activities.style: A Tudor merchant's house in inner-city Hackney
activities.whyGo: A 1535 Tudor house with original linenfold panelling, squatted and covered in punk murals in the 1980s - and the National Trust kept the graffiti alongside the panelling.
activities.opNote: The kept squat murals are the reason this is more interesting than an ordinary Tudor house. Limited opening days - check before travelling.

activities.name: Hackney Empire
activities.style: A surviving Frank Matcham music hall
activities.whyGo: Frank Matcham's 1901 music hall, gilded and tiered, where Chaplin and Stan Laurel played - and still the best pantomime in London every Christmas.
activities.opNote: Meets the theatre rule on this tab: the Matcham auditorium is the reason to go. The upper circle is cheap and the view from it is the best in the house.

activities.name: ArcelorMittal Orbit and the Slide
activities.style: Observation tower with the world's longest tunnel slide
activities.whyGo: Anish Kapoor's 114-metre tower, with the world's longest tunnel slide wrapped round it - 178 metres, twelve turns, forty seconds, at up to fifteen miles an hour.
activities.opNote: THE SLIDE HAS LIMITS: minimum age 8, minimum height 130cm, maximum weight 130kg, and under-18s need an adult. The viewing platform alone has no such restrictions.

activities.name: Queen Elizabeth Olympic Park
activities.style: The 2012 park, kept and replanted
activities.whyGo: 560 acres of the 2012 park with the waterways replanted, the Tumbling Bay playground, and free walking routes between every venue - the rare Olympic site that got a second life.
activities.opNote: Free and step-free throughout, which makes it one of the easiest large parks in London with a pushchair. Tumbling Bay Playground is free and excellent.

activities.name: London Aquatics Centre
activities.style: Public swimming in Zaha Hadid's Olympic pool
activities.whyGo: You can swim in the actual Olympic pool, under Zaha Hadid's wave of a roof, for the price of an ordinary council swim.
activities.opNote: A public leisure centre, not an attraction - book a lane swim online. The diving pool is separate and usually reserved for clubs.

activities.name: Lee Valley VeloPark
activities.style: Ride the Olympic velodrome
activities.address: Abercrombie Road, Queen Elizabeth Olympic Park
activities.whyGo: Book a taster session and ride the actual Olympic velodrome boards, or take the BMX track, mountain bike trails and road circuit outside it.
activities.opNote: Track sessions need booking and a short induction - you cannot just turn up and ride the velodrome. The outdoor trails are far more casual.

activities.name: London Stadium Tour
activities.style: Behind the scenes at the 2012 stadium
activities.whyGo: The dressing rooms, the players' tunnel and the pitchside seats of the stadium that held the 2012 opening ceremony, now West Ham's ground.
activities.opNote: Does not run on match days or event days, which is most weekends in season - check the fixture list before booking anything around it.

activities.name: Chelsea Physic Garden
activities.style: London's oldest botanic garden, founded 1673
activities.whyGo: Founded by the Apothecaries in 1673 to grow medicinal plants, and still growing 5,000 of them behind a high wall - with a microclimate warm enough for the northernmost outdoor grapefruit in Britain.
activities.opNote: Ticketed and walled, so it stays quiet even in summer. Closed for part of the winter - check before travelling. Best from April to July.

activities.name: Saatchi Gallery
activities.style: Contemporary art in the Duke of York's HQ
activities.address: Duke of York's HQ, King's Road
activities.whyGo: Seventy thousand square feet of white gallery in a former military headquarters, showing artists nobody has heard of yet - and most of it is free.
activities.opNote: Most exhibitions are free, though the big ticketed shows are not. The sculpture court outside on the King's Road is free and open to anyone.

activities.name: The King's Road
activities.style: The street the Sixties and punk both happened on
activities.whyGo: Mary Quant opened Bazaar here in 1955 and Vivienne Westwood and McLaren ran SEX at 430 in the seventies - two separate fashion revolutions on one road.
activities.opNote: Free to walk and about a mile end to end. Number 430 at the World's End end still has the backwards-running clock on the front.

activities.name: Royal Hospital Chelsea
activities.style: Wren's home for army veterans
activities.whyGo: Christopher Wren's 1692 hospital, still home to the Chelsea Pensioners in their scarlet coats, with Figure Court and the grounds open to walk into.
activities.opNote: The grounds, Figure Court and the small museum are free. The Chelsea Flower Show takes over the whole site for a week each May and the grounds shut.

activities.name: Camden Passage
activities.style: Antiques alley off Upper Street
activities.whyGo: A flagstoned alley off Upper Street lined with antique dealers, vintage shops and cafes - and nothing at all to do with Camden Town, which catches people out.
activities.opNote: The stalls come out on WEDNESDAYS AND SATURDAYS; the fixed shops trade most days. Not Camden - it is in Islington, a Tube ride away from the market people expect.

activities.name: Little Angel Theatre
activities.style: A puppet theatre in a converted temperance hall
activities.whyGo: A hundred-seat marionette theatre in a converted temperance hall down a passage, making its own puppets on site since 1961.
activities.opNote: Meets the theatre rule on this tab - a purpose-built puppet house rather than a playhouse. Shows are age-banded quite precisely; check before booking for a specific child.

activities.name: Regent's Canal at Islington
activities.style: Towpath walk either side of the Islington Tunnel
activities.whyGo: The towpath from City Road Basin west towards King's Cross, past narrowboats and the mouth of the 878-metre Islington Tunnel, which has no towpath through it at all.
activities.opNote: Free. The tunnel forces you up onto the street for about ten minutes - follow the marked diversion signs rather than assuming the towpath continues.

activities.name: Upper Street
activities.style: A mile of independents, bars and theatres
activities.whyGo: A mile from Angel to Highbury Corner, said to hold more restaurants and bars per yard than anywhere else in Britain, with independents and two theatres among them.
activities.opNote: Free to walk. The interesting part is the first half from Angel; the top end towards Highbury Corner thins out considerably.

activities.name: Maltby Street Market
activities.style: Weekend food market under railway arches
activities.whyGo: A narrow ropewalk of food traders wedged under the railway arches since 2010 - oysters, waffles, gin and a scotch egg stall with a permanent queue.
activities.opNote: WEEKENDS ONLY, and the alley is genuinely narrow - it is shoulder to shoulder by one o'clock on a Saturday. Go at opening or late afternoon.

activities.name: The Bermondsey Beer Mile
activities.style: Self-guided crawl of railway-arch breweries
activities.whyGo: A string of brewery taprooms in the railway arches running south-east from Maltby Street - unofficial, unbranded, and entirely walkable in an afternoon.
activities.opNote: SATURDAY is the day - most taprooms only open then, and a weekday attempt gets you shuttered arches. No booking, no ticket, and it is over-18 throughout.

activities.name: Fashion and Textile Museum
activities.style: The UK's only fashion and textile museum
activities.whyGo: Founded by Zandra Rhodes in a building she had painted hot pink and orange, and the only museum in Britain devoted to contemporary fashion and textile design.
activities.opNote: Exhibition-led, so there is no permanent display - if the current show does not appeal there is no reason to go. Closed between exhibitions, which catches people out.

activities.name: White Cube Bermondsey
activities.style: A vast free contemporary gallery
activities.whyGo: Fifty-four thousand square feet of gallery behind a plain Bermondsey Street frontage, showing major international artists - and free to walk into.
activities.opNote: Free, no booking, closed Mondays and Tuesdays. It is a commercial gallery, so the scale of the space surprises everyone who has not been.

activities.name: Lift 109
activities.style: Glass lift up a power station chimney
activities.whyGo: A glass lift that rises 109 metres up inside the north-west chimney of Battersea Power Station and out of the top, after a walk through the restored art deco Turbine Hall A.
activities.opNote: Timed tickets and the lift itself is only a few minutes - the history displays before it are most of the visit. Not one for anyone uneasy in a glass box.

activities.name: Battersea Power Station
activities.style: Shops and food inside a Grade II* power station
activities.whyGo: Gilbert Scott's brick cathedral of a power station, derelict for forty years, now holding 150 shops and restaurants with both original Turbine Halls opened up.
activities.opNote: Free to walk into, and worth it for Turbine Hall A's art deco alone even if you buy nothing. Its own Northern line station puts it fifteen minutes from the West End.

activities.name: Battersea Park
activities.style: Riverside Victorian park with a Peace Pagoda
activities.whyGo: Two hundred acres on the river with a boating lake, a Japanese Peace Pagoda on the Thames path and a bandstand - and the Power Station chimneys over the trees.
activities.opNote: Free. The riverside walk between the Peace Pagoda and Albert Bridge is the best bit and takes about twenty minutes.

activities.name: Battersea Park Children's Zoo
activities.style: A small zoo built for young children
activities.whyGo: Meerkats, monkeys, otters and a barnyard, scaled deliberately for under-tens - small enough to finish without anyone melting down.
activities.opNote: Much smaller and cheaper than London Zoo and better for very young children for exactly that reason. Reduced winter hours.

activities.name: Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew
activities.style: 300 acres and the largest living plant collection on earth
activities.whyGo: A World Heritage Site holding the largest collection of living plants anywhere, with the Palm House, the Temperate House and a treetop walkway eighteen metres up.
activities.opNote: Ticketed and cheaper booked online. It is 300 acres - allow half a day minimum and use the land train if walking is a problem.

activities.name: Richmond Park
activities.style: 2,500 acres of deer park
activities.whyGo: London's largest royal park, with about 600 free-roaming red and fallow deer, and a protected sightline from King Henry's Mound to St Paul's ten miles away.
activities.opNote: Free. KEEP AT LEAST 50 METRES FROM THE DEER, and further in the September-October rut and the May-July birthing season, when they are genuinely dangerous.

activities.name: Isabella Plantation
activities.style: Woodland garden inside Richmond Park
activities.whyGo: Forty acres of woodland garden walled inside Richmond Park, famous for evergreen azaleas and rhododendrons that peak in late April and early May.
activities.opNote: Free and inside the park, so there is no separate ticket. AZALEAS AND RHODODENDRONS, not roses - at least one guide has this wrong. Late April to mid-May is the window.

activities.name: The View from Richmond Hill
activities.style: The only view in England protected by an Act of Parliament
activities.whyGo: The bend of the Thames below Petersham Meadows, painted by Turner and Reynolds, and protected by its own Act of Parliament in 1902 - the only view in England that is.
activities.opNote: Free and reached on foot from Richmond station in about twenty minutes uphill. Best in the hour before sunset. Pubs and a terrace at the top.

activities.name: Petersham Nurseries
activities.style: Plant nursery with glasshouse dining
activities.whyGo: A working plant nursery down a lane off Petersham Meadows, with a teahouse and restaurant under the glasshouses and the plants left growing through the dining room.
activities.opNote: Free to walk round the nursery; the restaurant needs booking well ahead. Reached across Petersham Meadows from Richmond, which is a lovely twenty-minute walk.

activities.name: Hampstead Heath
activities.style: 790 acres of unmanicured heath
activities.whyGo: Seven hundred and ninety acres left deliberately wild, with Parliament Hill giving one of London's protected views - and unlike the royal parks, it feels like countryside.
activities.opNote: Free and open at all hours. It is genuinely easy to get lost - the paths are unsigned and the Heath is not laid out on a grid like a royal park.

activities.name: The Hampstead Bathing Ponds
activities.style: Open-water swimming, all year
activities.whyGo: Three lifeguarded natural ponds on the Heath - Men's, Ladies' and Mixed - open 365 days a year, including when there is ice on them.
activities.opNote: A small charge, and MINIMUM AGE 16 at the Men's and Ladies' ponds - under-16s are not admitted even with an adult. Unheated: winter water is close to freezing.

activities.name: Kenwood House
activities.style: A free Adam villa with a Vermeer in it
activities.whyGo: Robert Adam's library, and the Iveagh Bequest hanging in it - a Rembrandt self-portrait, a Vermeer and a Gainsborough - all of it free.
activities.opNote: FREE, which almost nobody expects of a house with those paintings in it. On the northern edge of the Heath, about twenty-five minutes uphill from Hampstead station.

activities.name: Highgate Cemetery
activities.style: Victorian cemetery with an Egyptian Avenue
activities.whyGo: Overgrown Victorian funerary architecture at its most theatrical - the Egyptian Avenue and the Circle of Lebanon on the West side, Marx and George Eliot on the East.
activities.opNote: Ticketed, and the WEST side is by guided tour only - the Egyptian Avenue is on that side, so a ticket for the East side alone does not get you to the famous part.

activities.name: The Prospect of Whitby
activities.style: London's oldest riverside pub
activities.whyGo: Standing since about 1520, with a flagstone floor, a pewter-topped bar on old barrels and a replica gallows on the river terrace where Judge Jeffreys drank.
activities.opNote: Free to walk into. The back terrace over the river is far better than the front bar and is where you want to sit - go round rather than stopping at the door.

activities.name: Wapping Thames Path and the Old Stairs
activities.style: Riverside walk down to the foreshore
activities.whyGo: Wapping Old Stairs and Pelican Stairs are medieval river accesses still there between the warehouses, and at low tide they put you on the actual Thames foreshore.
activities.opNote: Free. CHECK THE TIDE TABLE - the foreshore is only there at low water and the Thames comes in fast. The stairs are steep, slippery and unlit.

activities.name: Tobacco Dock
activities.style: Grade I warehouse turned events space
activities.whyGo: A Grade I listed 1811 tobacco warehouse with brick vaults and iron columns, now an events space holding up to ten thousand, with a roof garden over the top.
activities.opNote: The building is the point. Free to walk through when nothing is on, ticketed when there is - so check the events listing before setting out either way.

activities.name: Frank's Cafe
activities.style: Summer bar on top of a car park
activities.whyGo: A bar under a red tarpaulin on the top deck of a Rye Lane multi-storey car park, with an uninterrupted view north to St Paul's and the City for the price of a negroni.
activities.opNote: SUMMER ONLY, roughly May to September - turning up to a closed car park in November is the single most common Peckham mistake. No booking; the stair queue moves.

activities.name: Bold Tendencies
activities.style: Free sculpture commissions on a car park roof
activities.whyGo: A non-profit that has been commissioning sculpture, opera and orchestral performance on the top floors of a Peckham car park since 2007 - and the art is free to see.
activities.opNote: Free and summer only, on the same floors as Frank's. The classical and opera programme is ticketed but cheap; the sculpture costs nothing.

activities.name: Peckham Levels
activities.style: Studios, food and bars in the lower car park floors
activities.whyGo: Seven floors of the same Rye Lane car park turned into studios, food traders and bars - and unlike Frank's above it, it stays open all year.
activities.opNote: Free to walk into and OPEN YEAR-ROUND, which is the difference between it and the rooftop. Lift access to every floor.

activities.name: The Bussey Building
activities.style: Arts and nightlife in a cricket bat factory
activities.whyGo: A Victorian cricket bat factory off Rye Lane holding club nights, a rooftop, a cinema and studios - the anchor of Peckham's night economy.
activities.opNote: Over-18 for the club nights, mixed use in the day. Copeland Park around it holds bars and food and is free to walk into.

activities.name: South London Gallery
activities.style: Free contemporary art on Peckham Road
activities.whyGo: Free contemporary art across two sites - the original Victorian gallery and a converted fire station opposite - with a good garden behind the main building.
activities.opNote: Free, closed Mondays. The garden and the cafe are open without going into the exhibitions at all.

activities.name: Peckhamplex
activities.style: Current releases at a fraction of West End prices
activities.whyGo: An independent cinema showing current releases for a few pounds a seat, which in central London would buy you roughly a fifth of a ticket.
activities.opNote: Meets the cinema rule on VALUE rather than the room - the price is genuinely the story, and it is a local institution defended fiercely whenever redevelopment is mentioned.

activities.name: Flight Club Bloomsbury
activities.style: Social darts in private oches
activities.whyGo: Cameras track every dart to sub-millimetre accuracy and run the scoring for you, so nobody needs to be able to play or add up.
activities.opNote: Booked by the oche rather than per head, so a full group is much better value. Under-18s are admitted only at limited daytime slots.

activities.name: Flight Club Shoreditch
activities.style: Social darts in private oches
activities.whyGo: The original of the format, in the Alphabeta Building - automated scoring, a fairground-parlour interior and games designed to keep everyone in until the end.
activities.opNote: Sells out weeks ahead for Thursday and Friday evenings. Book the oche, not seats.

activities.name: Flight Club Islington
activities.style: Social darts in private oches
activities.whyGo: Automated social darts on Upper Street, which puts it inside a mile of more restaurants per yard than anywhere else in Britain.
activities.opNote: Booked by the oche. Upper Street means you can eat anywhere afterwards without moving the group far.

activities.name: Flight Club Victoria
activities.style: Social darts in private oches
activities.whyGo: The one genuinely fun thing to do around Victoria, in an area otherwise built entirely around getting people onto trains.
activities.opNote: Two minutes from Victoria station, which makes it the easy choice when a group is arriving from different directions.

activities.name: NQ64 Soho
activities.style: Retro arcade and cocktail bar
activities.whyGo: A dark basement of arcade cabinets and console booths played on tokens, with cocktails named after video games - and no booking needed.
