activities.opNote: Over-18 at all times. Walk-in, which makes it the rare activity bar you can use on a whim; queues form late at weekends.

activities.name: NQ64 Shoreditch
activities.style: Retro arcade and cocktail bar
activities.whyGo: Arcade cabinets, Mario Kart booths and a token machine on Old Street, open late and free to walk into.
activities.opNote: Over-18 throughout, walk-in, and no charge to get in - you pay for tokens and drinks only.

activities.name: Swingers West End
activities.style: 1920s seaside crazy golf and street food
activities.whyGo: Three crazy golf courses done as a 1920s British seaside, with five bars, five street food traders and a roof terrace, a minute off Oxford Circus.
activities.opNote: Over-18 in the evening; there are limited family sessions. Street food is from named traders rather than a single kitchen.

activities.name: Swingers City
activities.style: Crazy golf under the Gherkin
activities.whyGo: Two nine-hole courses, four street food traders and five bars in a two-storey clubhouse a stone's throw from the Gherkin.
activities.opNote: Books out with office parties from Thursday onwards - a weekday lunchtime or a weekend is far easier to get.

activities.name: Rocket Room
activities.style: Axe throwing, darts and shuffleboard
activities.whyGo: The only axe throwing in Leicester Square, on a second floor above the crowds, with purpose-built lanes plus interactive darts and shuffleboard.
activities.opNote: Over-18 throughout for the axe lanes. Closed-toe shoes are required - people are turned away in sandals.

activities.name: Roxy Ball Room St Mary Axe
activities.style: Duckpin bowling and eight other games
activities.whyGo: Duckpin bowling, ice-free curling, tech darts, American pool, ping pong and karaoke rooms under one roof beside the Gherkin.
activities.opNote: The point is the range - a group that cannot agree on one game can play six. Book the activity, not a table.

activities.name: Lane7 Victoria
activities.style: Bowling, mini golf and a basement arcade
activities.whyGo: Bowling, crazy golf, beer pong, interactive darts and a hidden basement arcade - the widest spread of games in this half of Westminster.
activities.opNote: Family-friendly in the day and over-18 in the evening; check the switchover before bringing children after work.

activities.name: Clays The City
activities.style: Virtual clay shooting and cocktails
activities.whyGo: Clay pigeon shooting reworked as a simulator game in a cocktail bar - you shoot at screens, and it is far more absorbing than that sounds.
activities.opNote: Ninety-minute slots for up to twenty, over-18 only, three minutes from Moorgate. Clarified cocktails are the bar's own thing.

activities.name: Clays Canary Wharf
activities.style: Virtual clay shooting and cocktails
activities.whyGo: The same simulated shooting format two minutes from Canary Wharf station, which is why it is booked solid with office parties from Thursday.
activities.opNote: Over-18 only. Weekday evenings go to corporate bookings; weekends are far easier and quieter here than in the City.

activities.name: F1 Arcade
activities.style: Full-motion F1 simulators and a bar
activities.whyGo: Sixty-odd full-motion racing simulators in seventeen thousand square feet at One New Change, with the dome of St Paul's through the windows.
activities.opNote: Races are scored across the room, so you are competing with strangers as well as your group. Over-18 in the evening.

activities.name: Sixes Social Cricket Fitzrovia
activities.style: Batting nets with a bar attached
activities.whyGo: Private batting nets that bowl at you and score automatically, so it works for people who have never held a bat - and the food is a proper kitchen, not an afterthought.
activities.opNote: Booked by the net for up to twelve. Family-friendly in the day, which is unusual in this category.

activities.name: Sixes Social Cricket Shoreditch
activities.style: Batting nets with a bar attached
activities.whyGo: The Rivington Street site, in the middle of Shoreditch's bar run, so the net is the start of the evening rather than all of it.
activities.opNote: Booked by the net. Rivington Street means everything else is a two-minute walk when you finish.

activities.name: Sixes Social Cricket London Bridge
activities.style: Batting nets with a bar attached
activities.whyGo: On Bermondsey Street itself, which makes it the one bookable group activity on a street otherwise made of restaurants and galleries.
activities.opNote: Booked by the net for up to twelve. Family-friendly during the day.

activities.name: Draughts Waterloo
activities.style: Board game cafe and bar
activities.whyGo: Over a thousand board games, a small cover charge to play as many as you like, and staff whose job is to teach you the rules.
activities.opNote: On Leake Street, the graffiti tunnel under Waterloo - which is worth walking through on the way. Book a table at weekends.

activities.name: Draughts Stratford
activities.style: Board game cafe and bar
activities.whyGo: The newer of the two sites, on the Olympic Park by the Aquatics Centre, with the same thousand-game library and rules-explaining staff.
activities.opNote: Opened 2025. A cover charge per person to play, on top of food and drink. Good rainy-day answer on the Olympic Park.

activities.name: Hay's Galleria
activities.style: Victorian wharf under a glass barrel roof
activities.whyGo: Hay's Wharf, where Britain's tea came ashore, roofed over in 1987 with a glass and steel barrel vault modelled on Milan's Galleria Vittorio Emanuele II - and holding David Kemp's sixty-foot kinetic sculpture The Navigators.
activities.opNote: Free, covered and open to walk through, which makes it the best wet-weather stop on the riverside between London Bridge and Tower Bridge. The Navigators moves and squirts water on the hour.

activities.name: Outernet London
activities.style: Four-storey wraparound LED halls
activities.whyGo: Four-storey 16K screens wrapping the walls and ceiling of a public hall by Tottenham Court Road - you walk in off the street, for nothing, and stand inside the picture.
activities.opNote: FREE and no booking. The content changes constantly, so it is worth a look whenever you pass rather than a planned trip. The music venue underneath is ticketed; the screen halls are not.

activities.name: Bunga 90
activities.style: Interactive 1990s bar with karaoke and arcades
activities.whyGo: A 1990s world built out in full - a working video rental store, arcade cabinets, karaoke rooms and cocktails in novelty glasses - rather than a bar with a few posters up.
activities.opNote: Over-18. Booked in sections; the karaoke rooms go separately from the main floor. Drury Lane, so it is a two-minute walk from the Piazza.

activities.name: Cahoots
activities.style: A 1940s Underground station, in character
activities.whyGo: A disused 1940s Tube station rebuilt underneath Kingly Court, complete with a carriage, ration-book menus and staff who stay in character all night.
activities.opNote: Over-18 and booked in advance - it is not a walk-in. Playing along is expected; the staff will not drop the act if you do not.

activities.name: The Garden Cinema
activities.style: Art deco arthouse with 35mm
activities.whyGo: Three small screens and two art deco bars on a back street between Holborn and Covent Garden, running repertory seasons and 35mm prints alongside new releases.
activities.opNote: Opened 2022 and independent. Screens hold 40, 60 and 70, so seasons sell out. Post-screening talks with filmmakers are a regular part of the programme, not an occasional event.

activities.name: Prince Charles Cinema
activities.style: Cult repertory, sing-alongs and all-nighters
activities.whyGo: The cult cinema of London - 35mm and 70mm prints, quote-alongs, sing-alongs and all-night marathons, a hundred yards from the Leicester Square multiplexes and a fraction of the price.
activities.opNote: Membership is cheap and pays for itself in about two visits. Sing-along and marathon screenings sell out months ahead; ordinary showings rarely do.

activities.name: Regent Street Cinema
activities.style: The birthplace of British cinema
activities.whyGo: Where the Lumière brothers' Cinematographe had its first British showing in 1896 - the birthplace of cinema in this country, still running with Super 8, 16mm and 35mm projectors.
activities.opNote: Inside the University of Westminster, so the entrance reads as a university building rather than a cinema. Built as a theatre in 1848.

activities.name: Rio Cinema
activities.style: Art deco single screen, community-run
activities.whyGo: A century of continuous operation on Kingsland High Street, in a preserved art deco auditorium run as a charity, with late-night cult screenings and a strong queer programme.
activities.opNote: Single main screen, so the programme is genuinely curated rather than a grid. Not-for-profit - the ticket money stays in the building.

activities.name: The Castle Cinema
activities.style: Crowdfunded cinema above a bookmaker
activities.whyGo: A 1913 cinema that became a bingo hall, a shoe factory and a snooker club before Clapton crowdfunded it back into a cinema in 2017 - sofas, a bar, and a registered charity.
activities.opNote: Up a staircase above a shop, so access is limited. Book ahead - it is small and local, and weekend evenings go.

activities.name: Frameless
activities.style: Immersive digital art across four galleries
activities.whyGo: Forty-two paintings - Monet, Van Gogh, Dalí, Rembrandt - blown up across four rooms of floor-to-ceiling projection, with mirrored floors and motion sensors that let you push the pictures around.
activities.opNote: Timed tickets, step-free throughout, and the UK's largest permanent venue of its kind. It is a projection experience, not a collection - there are no actual paintings in the building.

activities.name: Lightroom
activities.style: Four-storey projection auditorium
activities.whyGo: A purpose-built four-storey room where the show runs on every wall and the floor at once - one production at a time, properly made, rather than a rolling loop.
activities.opNote: Runs a single production for months at a time, so what is on decides whether it is worth going. Timed tickets and fully step-free.

activities.name: Sir John Soane's Museum
activities.style: An architect's house, left exactly as he died in it
activities.whyGo: Soane's own house, preserved by Act of Parliament exactly as he left it in 1837 - mirrors, top-lit wells, Hogarth's Rake's Progress on hinged panels, and a sarcophagus in the basement.
activities.opNote: FREE, which almost nobody expects. Small and dark by design, so entry is limited and timed slots are worth booking. Narrow stairs; not accessible.

activities.name: The Postal Museum and Mail Rail
activities.style: Ride the underground postal railway
activities.whyGo: A miniature train ride through the actual tunnels of the Post Office's own underground railway, closed in 2003 and reopened with passenger cars built to fit.
activities.opNote: The Mail Rail ride is a separate timed ticket from the museum and sells out first. The cars are small and enclosed - not for anyone uneasy in confined spaces.

activities.name: The Old Operating Theatre Museum
activities.style: A Georgian surgical theatre in a church attic
activities.whyGo: The oldest surviving surgical theatre in Europe, in the roof space of a church by London Bridge, reached up a 52-step spiral staircase - operating table, sawdust box and all.
activities.opNote: The spiral staircase is the only way in and there is no lift, which makes it genuinely inaccessible. Weekend surgery demonstrations are the thing to time a visit around.

activities.name: Wilton's Music Hall
activities.style: The oldest surviving grand music hall in the world
activities.whyGo: The oldest grand music hall left standing anywhere, saved from demolition and conserved rather than restored - the peeling walls and bare brick were deliberately left as found.
activities.opNote: The Mahogany Bar is open some evenings without a ticket, which is the cheapest way to see the building. Down an alley off Cable Street and very easy to walk past.

activities.name: The 100 Club
activities.style: A basement on Oxford Street since 1942
activities.whyGo: The same basement since 1942 - trad jazz, then the Rolling Stones, then the 1976 Punk Festival that launched the Sex Pistols and the Clash in one weekend.
activities.opNote: A low basement with pillars, so sightlines are poor from the back - get down the front or accept you are there for the sound and the room.

activities.name: Union Chapel
activities.style: Gigs in a working Gothic chapel
activities.whyGo: A working Victorian Gothic chapel that puts on gigs from the pews, with an organ behind the stage and acoustics no purpose-built venue in London can match.
activities.opNote: Still an active church and a homeless drop-in centre, and ticket money funds both. Pews, so seated and not especially comfortable - that is part of it.

activities.name: MOTH Club
activities.style: Gigs in a working veterans' social club
activities.whyGo: A Memorable Order of Tin Hats veterans' club with a gold-tinsel stage curtain, still run as a members' social club by day and one of London's best 250-capacity rooms by night.
activities.opNote: Over-18. The tinsel curtain and the regimental plaques are not a theme - it is a real veterans' club that happens to book excellent bands.

activities.name: ALCOTRAZ
activities.style: Prison-themed cocktail experience
activities.whyGo: You are processed on arrival, issued an orange jumpsuit and an inmate number, and have to smuggle your own spirit past the guards - they mix it into whatever you are given.
activities.opNote: BRING YOUR OWN SPIRIT - that is the format, and people arrive without one. Over-18. Running since 2017, so it is the established one of this group.

activities.name: Hexmoor
activities.style: Wizarding prison cocktail bar
activities.whyGo: The same jumpsuit-and-cell format as Alcotraz next door, rebuilt as a wizarding prison with practical effects and cocktails that behave oddly.
activities.opNote: Opened September 2025, so it is the newest of the three and the hardest to book. Over-18.

activities.name: AVORA
activities.style: Bioluminescent off-world cocktail bar
activities.whyGo: An alien planet built out in full - bioluminescent planting, creatures and a bar - and the best-looking of the three Hoxton shows by some distance.
activities.opNote: Over-18, 105 minutes, booked in advance. The visual build is the reason to pick this one over Alcotraz or Hexmoor.

activities.name: Moonshine Saloon
activities.style: Prohibition-era Wild West cocktail experience
activities.whyGo: A Wild West saloon where you help run the still - the cocktails are made in front of you as part of the story rather than brought to a table.
activities.opNote: Over-18. At the Aldgate edge of the City rather than the middle, so allow a walk from Bank or Liverpool Street.

activities.name: Boom Lab
activities.style: Video-game style team adventure
activities.whyGo: Built like a video game rather than an escape room - rooms of physical challenges scored against the clock, with a lab conceit holding it together.
activities.opNote: Family-friendly in the day. Physical rather than puzzle-led, so it suits groups who bounce off escape rooms.

activities.name: BuzzAttack
activities.style: Playable television game show
activities.whyGo: A game show run for your group with a live host, buzzers and a scoreboard - the format THE CUBE does for Canary Wharf, done in Hoxton.
activities.opNote: Team-based and hosted, so it needs a group rather than a couple.

activities.name: Race Across The World: The Experience
activities.style: Timed puzzle race through real streets
activities.whyGo: The television format played outdoors - checkpoints, a budget and a clock, run through streets you would otherwise just be walking down.
activities.opNote: Partly outdoors, so dress for weather. Two London routes exist and they are different games, not the same one twice.

activities.name: Race Across The World: The Experience, City
activities.style: Timed puzzle race through real streets
activities.whyGo: The City route, which uses the alleys and churchyards most people walk past - a better way to see the Square Mile than a walking tour.
activities.opNote: A different route from the West End version. Partly outdoors.

activities.name: The Paddington Bear Experience
activities.style: Walk-through family adventure
activities.whyGo: A walk-through Paddington adventure built for small children - the Browns' house, the marmalade, and enough to do that under-sixes stay interested.
activities.opNote: At WATERLOO, not Paddington, which catches out almost everyone who books it. Timed tickets.

activities.name: Faulty Towers: The Dining Experience
activities.style: Comedy dinner theatre
activities.whyGo: A three-course dinner served by Basil, Sybil and Manuel entirely in character, with about seventy per cent of it improvised around the room.
activities.opNote: Running for decades and in a hotel near Russell Square. You are part of the show whether or not you want to be.

activities.name: The Murdér Express
activities.style: Murder mystery over dinner on a train set
activities.whyGo: A 1930s dining car built inside a railway arch, a four-course dinner, and a murder to solve between courses.
activities.opNote: Three hours and a full dinner, so it is the evening rather than the start of it. Over-18.

activities.name: David Bowie: You're Not Alone
activities.style: Multimedia Bowie retrospective
activities.whyGo: A projected retrospective built round the Bowie archive, which the V&A acquired and brought to King's Cross.
activities.opNote: Listed as open-ended, but archive shows of this kind rarely stay forever - check before travelling for it specifically.

activities.name: Colosseum: The Legendary Arena
activities.style: VR reconstruction of Roman Rome
activities.whyGo: A headset reconstruction of the Colosseum as it stood, walked rather than watched, in a Camden venue that also runs the ISS experience.
activities.opNote: Headset-based, so it does not suit anyone prone to motion sickness. Book a slot.

activities.name: Space Explorers: The ISS Experience
activities.style: Free-roaming VR aboard the space station
activities.whyGo: Free-roaming VR filmed aboard the actual International Space Station, so you walk the modules rather than sitting in a chair looking around.
activities.opNote: Free-roam means you move through a real room in a headset - more physical than seated VR, and better for it.

activities.name: Smithsonian Starstruck
activities.style: Space exploration VR
activities.whyGo: A Smithsonian-built space experience in the museum quarter, which is the obvious place for it and yet the only paid one of its kind on that street.
activities.opNote: Ticketed, unlike the three free national museums either side of it.
